content.title: HR Employee Onboarding Plan
content.summary: Comprehensive onboarding plan for a beginner HR role in People Operations, addressing key mandatory and encouraged requirements due within the first 90 days.

items.source_quote: Employees must acknowledge the current handbook within 1 working day of joining. If access is unavailable, HR records the outage and obtains a supervised paper acknowledgement within the same period.
items.learning_objective: Learn to ensure all employees acknowledge the current handbook within 1 working day, and handle exceptions if electronic access is unavailable.
items.practical_activity: Simulate an employee joining scenario where you must document handbook acknowledgement electronically or via supervised paper if digital access fails.
items.lesson: It is mandatory to ensure that every new employee acknowledges the current handbook within 1 working day of their joining date. If the employee cannot access the handbook electronically, HR must record this outage and obtain a supervised paper acknowledgement within the same time frame. This process secures compliance and accurate record-keeping for employee orientation.
checklist: Verify employee receipt of the current handbook on Day 1.
Confirm electronic access to the handbook.
If access is unavailable, record the outage immediately.
Obtain and document a supervised paper acknowledgement within 1 working day.

scenario.prompt: A new employee reports no access to the digital employee handbook on their joining day. How do you proceed to ensure compliance?
scenario.expected_response: You record the access outage and promptly obtain a supervised paper handbook acknowledgement from the employee all within 1 working day.

quiz.question: What must HR do if a new employee cannot access the digital handbook within 1 working day?
options: Record the outage and obtain a supervised paper acknowledgement within the same period.
Wait until the next week to follow up.
Ignore and proceed without acknowledgement.
Send email reminders until electronic acknowledgement is received.
quiz.explanation: Since electronic acknowledgement is unavailable, HR is required to record the outage and obtain a supervised paper acknowledgement within 1 working day.
quiz.evidence_quote: Employees must acknowledge the current handbook within 1 working day of joining. If access is unavailable, HR records the outage and obtains a supervised paper acknowledgement within the same period.

rubric.criterion: Accurately explains the handbook acknowledgement procedure in the scenario.
Completes the practical activity documenting both electronic and paper acknowledgements correctly.
Demonstrates timely completion within 1 working day.

items.source_quote: Employees must notify the manager as soon as reasonably possible when an emergency prevents attendance. Where the employee cannot communicate, HR must accept notification from a nominated contact and record the circumstances.
items.learning_objective: Understand proper procedures for managing employee emergency absences, including manager notification and HR's role when direct communication is impossible.
items.practical_activity: Create a mock log of an emergency absence reported by a nominated contact and practice recording details accurately.
items.lesson: When an employee cannot attend work due to an emergency, they are required to notify their manager as soon as reasonably possible. If the employee is unable to communicate directly, HR must accept notification from a nominated contact and carefully record the circumstances. This ensures timely awareness and proper documentation of unexpected absences to maintain operational continuity.
checklist: Ensure employees know the importance of notifying their manager promptly.
Accept absence notifications from nominated contacts when employee cannot communicate.
Record all relevant details and circumstances of the emergency absence.
Notify the relevant parties and update absence records promptly.

scenario.prompt: An employee is hospitalized and cannot inform their manager. A family member contacts HR to report the absence. What steps should HR take?
scenario.expected_response: HR accepts the notification from the nominated contact, documents the circumstances fully, and informs the manager accordingly.

quiz.question: If an employee cannot notify their manager about an emergency absence, what must HR do?
options: Accept notification from a nominated contact and record the circumstances.
Delay notification until the employee recovers.
Notate absence only after employee returns.
Wait for manager to find out independently.
quiz.explanation: HR's responsibility is to accept notification from a nominated contact if the employee cannot communicate and to record the circumstances accurately.
quiz.evidence_quote: Employees must notify the manager as soon as reasonably possible when an emergency prevents attendance. Where the employee cannot communicate, HR must accept notification from a nominated contact and record the circumstances.

rubric.criterion: Demonstrates understanding of notification procedure in emergency absence.
Accurately documents absence based on nominated contact information.
Completes practice log clearly and timely.

items.source_quote: Managers must review employee readiness by the end of the first 30 calendar days and document remaining gaps, supervised-work limits and follow-up dates.
items.learning_objective: Learn how to evaluate and document an employee's readiness within the first 30 days, identifying gaps and planning follow-ups.
items.practical_activity: Simulate a readiness review meeting and create a documented report listing gaps, any supervised work limits, and scheduled follow-up dates.
items.lesson: Managers are required to conduct a review of each employee's readiness by the end of the first 30 calendar days. This review must include documentation of any remaining skill or knowledge gaps, limits on supervised work, and planned follow-up activities or dates. HR supports managers in ensuring timely and accurate readiness assessments to facilitate employee development and performance management.
checklist: Schedule readiness review meeting before end of 30 days.
Collect manager's assessments of employee skills and work limits.
Document findings clearly, including gaps and supervised work restrictions.
Plan and record follow-up dates for ongoing development or reassessment.

scenario.prompt: You are assisting a manager preparing the first 30-day readiness review for a new hire. What key information should be included in the report?
scenario.expected_response: The report should detail remaining knowledge or skill gaps, any supervised-work limits, and agreed follow-up dates.

quiz.question: What must managers document during the employee readiness review by day 30?
options: Remaining gaps, supervised-work limits, and follow-up dates.
Only employee strengths.
Employee attendance records.
Salary adjustments and promotions.
quiz.explanation: Managers must document any remaining gaps, limits on supervised work, and scheduled follow-up dates during the readiness review.
quiz.evidence_quote: Managers must review employee readiness by the end of the first 30 calendar days and document remaining gaps, supervised-work limits and follow-up dates.

rubric.criterion: Identifies and documents employee gaps and work limits correctly.
Creates a clear, actionable readiness review report.
Schedules appropriate follow-up dates within the plan.

items.source_quote: Record owners are encouraged to review archive searchability quarterly and propose improvements to naming or indexing.
items.module_title: Quarterly Archive Searchability and Improvement Suggestions
items.learning_objective: Encourage understanding of archive management by conducting quarterly reviews of searchability and recommending naming or indexing improvements.
items.practical_activity: Conduct a mock quarterly archive review and draft proposals to improve naming conventions and indexing methods.
items.lesson: Record owners are encouraged, but not mandated, to review archive searchability on a quarterly basis. They should propose improvements to naming or indexing to enhance the accessibility and efficiency of record retrieval. This practice supports ongoing improvement of the archive system and helps maintain organized and easily searchable records.
checklist: Review current archive search functions and results.
Identify potential areas for improved naming or indexing.
Draft proposals for suggested improvements.
Submit recommendations to the archive management team.

scenario.prompt: You complete a quarterly review of the archive searchability. What should you do with your findings?
scenario.expected_response: You should propose improvements to naming or indexing based on identified issues or opportunities for better search results.

quiz.question: What are record owners encouraged to do quarterly?
options: Review archive searchability and propose improvements.
Delete outdated archives.
Ignore archive systems.
Outsource archive management.
quiz.explanation: Record owners are encouraged to review archive searchability quarterly and suggest improvements to naming or indexing, enhancing efficiency.
quiz.evidence_quote: Record owners are encouraged to review archive searchability quarterly and propose improvements to naming or indexing.

rubric.criterion: Correctly identifies archive searchability issues.
Proposes relevant and actionable improvements.
Completes review and report within required time frame.

items.source_quote: Employees must store operational evidence in the approved case or document repository. A local copy must not become the sole record of a decision or transaction.
items.learning_objective: Understand and apply the correct procedures for storing operational evidence in approved repositories to ensure data integrity and compliance.
items.practical_activity: Simulate storing operational evidence by uploading a sample document to the approved repository. Confirm that no local copies serve as the only record.
items.lesson: Storing operational evidence securely is essential to protect organizational data and maintain compliance. You must always save such evidence in the approved case or document repository, ensuring it is the official record. Keeping only local copies is not permitted, as local copies cannot replace the official records and risk data loss or integrity issues. Proper use of the repository facilitates transparency, accessibility, and audit readiness.
checklist: Locate and access the approved document repository.
Upload a sample operational evidence document to the repository.
Verify no local copy remains as the only record.
Confirm correct categorization and metadata are applied.

scenario.prompt: You find a signed contract on your local computer from a recent negotiation. What should you do?
scenario.expected_response: Upload the contract to the approved document repository immediately. Ensure the repository copy is the official record. Delete any local copies to prevent confusion or data loss.

quiz.question: What is the correct procedure regarding operational evidence storage?
options: Store all evidence only in the approved repository, never relying on local copies as the sole record.
Keep a local copy as the sole record for quick access.
Emails can serve as the sole record of decisions.
It is acceptable to save work documents only locally if backed up.
quiz.explanation: Employees must store operational evidence in the approved case or document repository. A local copy must not become the sole record of a decision or transaction.
quiz.evidence_quote: Employees must store operational evidence in the approved case or document repository. A local copy must not become the sole record of a decision or transaction.

rubric.criterion: Accuracy of repository upload and elimination of sole local copy
Completeness of scenario response regarding correct storage procedures
Clarity and adherence to checklist steps in the practical activity

items.source_quote: Employees must stop an unintended transfer where possible and report suspected disclosure through POL-09 immediately. They must preserve evidence and must not conceal or silently delete the incident history.
items.learning_objective: Learn how to identify, stop, report, and preserve evidence of accidental data disclosures according to company policy POL-09.
items.practical_activity: Review a simulated accidental disclosure scenario; draft a report using the POL-09 reporting format and list steps to preserve incident evidence.
items.lesson: Accidental disclosure of sensitive information can jeopardize the company and individuals. Employees must act swiftly to stop any unintended data transfer when possible. It is mandatory to report suspected disclosures immediately through POL-09, preserving all evidence related to the incident. Concealing or silently deleting incident history is strictly prohibited. Handling such situations carefully helps mitigate risks and ensures accountability.
checklist: Identify and attempt to halt any unintended data transfers.
Prepare an incident report using POL-09 guidelines.
Preserve all evidence related to the disclosure incident.
Do not delete or conceal any related incident data or history.

scenario.prompt: You accidentally sent confidential data to the wrong contact. What steps should you take?
scenario.expected_response: Immediately stop any further sending if possible. Report the incident using POL-09 immediately, preserving all relevant evidence without deleting any incident history.

quiz.question: If you suspect an accidental data disclosure, what must you do?
options: Stop the transfer if possible and report immediately through POL-09 preserving all evidence.
Ignore if it seems minor and fix it later.
Delete all related emails to avoid detection.
Wait to see if the issue escalates before reporting.
quiz.explanation: Employees must stop an unintended transfer where possible and report suspected disclosure through POL-09 immediately. They must preserve evidence and must not conceal or silently delete the incident history.
quiz.evidence_quote: Employees must stop an unintended transfer where possible and report suspected disclosure through POL-09 immediately. They must preserve evidence and must not conceal or silently delete the incident history.

rubric.criterion: Effectiveness of incident stoppage and reporting
Quality and completeness of POL-09 incident report drafted
Demonstrated understanding of evidence preservation and reporting integrity

items.source_quote: Employees must communicate respectfully and must not harass, threaten or discriminate against another person. A witness must report concerns through the confidential HR channel without circulating the allegation to colleagues.
items.learning_objective: Identify respectful communication norms and correct procedures for confidential reporting of workplace behavior concerns.
items.practical_activity: Role-play a scenario involving witnessing inappropriate conduct and draft a confidential report to HR without discussing with colleagues.
items.lesson: Respectful communication is fundamental in maintaining a positive workplace. All employees must avoid harassment, threats, and discrimination. If you witness inappropriate behavior, you must report it through the confidential HR channels only, without circulating the allegation among colleagues. This preserves victim confidentiality and avoids workplace tension. Upholding these standards supports a healthy and inclusive work environment for everyone.
checklist: Always use respectful language in all communications.
Do not harass, threaten, or discriminate against colleagues.
If witnessing concerns, report through the confidential HR channel.
Refrain from discussing allegations with other employees.

scenario.prompt: You overhear a coworker making discriminatory remarks. What should you do?
scenario.expected_response: Report the concern through the confidential HR channel immediately, without discussing the matter with other colleagues.

quiz.question: What is the correct approach if you witness harassment at work?
options: Report through confidential HR channels without sharing details with others.
Discuss the issue openly with colleagues to gather support.
Ignore the behavior if unsure.
Post concerns anonymously on social media.
quiz.explanation: Employees must communicate respectfully and must not harass, threaten or discriminate against another person. A witness must report concerns through the confidential HR channel without circulating the allegation to colleagues.
quiz.evidence_quote: Employees must communicate respectfully and must not harass, threaten or discriminate against another person. A witness must report concerns through the confidential HR channel without circulating the allegation to colleagues.

rubric.criterion: Appropriateness of communication tone in role-play
Accuracy of confidential reporting process
Adherence to checklist steps and confidentiality principles

items.source_quote: The HR Executive must schedule core orientation within POL-03 deadlines and monitor attendance. A missed session requires a replacement assignment and visible overdue status where relevant.
items.learning_objective: Ensure timely scheduling and monitoring of orientation sessions, and handle missed sessions according to policy.
items.practical_activity: Create a sample orientation schedule within POL-03 deadlines, track attendance, and plan a replacement for a missed session including status tracking.
items.lesson: As an HR Executive, you must schedule core orientation sessions within the timelines specified by POL-03. Monitoring attendance is critical: if someone misses a session, you must arrange a replacement promptly. Additionally, the missed attendance and replacement must be visibly tracked, such as using an overdue status indicator where relevant. These steps ensure new employees receive essential onboarding without delay and maintain compliance with company policies.
checklist: Review POL-03 orientation scheduling deadlines.
Schedule orientation session within required deadlines.
Monitor attendance during sessions.
Arrange replacement and mark overdue status for missed attendance.

scenario.prompt: An employee missed the scheduled orientation session. What are your next actions?
scenario.expected_response: Schedule a replacement orientation session promptly and ensure the missed session shows a visible overdue status as required.

quiz.question: What must HR do if an employee misses core orientation?
options: Assign a replacement session and ensure visible overdue status.
Ignore the absence if justified.
Cancel the orientation for the employee.
Reschedule only if requested by the employee.
quiz.explanation: The HR Executive must schedule core orientation within POL-03 deadlines and monitor attendance. A missed session requires a replacement assignment and visible overdue status where relevant.
quiz.evidence_quote: The HR Executive must schedule core orientation within POL-03 deadlines and monitor attendance. A missed session requires a replacement assignment and visible overdue status where relevant.

rubric.criterion: Timeliness and compliance of orientation scheduling
Effectiveness of attendance monitoring and replacement planning
Visibility and accuracy of overdue status tracking

items.source_quote: Employees must score at least 80 percent on mandatory knowledge assessments. A failed attempt requires targeted revision and another attempt; the original result must remain recorded.
items.learning_objective: Ensure HR understands the knowledge assessment standard and procedures on failure for compliance.
items.practical_activity: Complete a simulated mandatory knowledge assessment with an 80% passing threshold. If unsuccessful, draft a targeted revision plan and retake the assessment, ensuring documentation of all attempts.
items.lesson: Employees are required to achieve a minimum score of 80% on mandatory knowledge assessments. If the first attempt is unsuccessful, employees must undertake targeted revision before a subsequent attempt. All results, including failed attempts, must be permanently recorded without alteration. This ensures continued compliance and accurate recordkeeping for skill verification.
checklist: Review mandatory knowledge assessment content and format.
Understand the 80% minimum passing score requirement.
Learn the procedure for targeted revision after failing.
Know how to document all assessment attempts accurately.

scenario.prompt: You took the mandatory knowledge assessment and scored 75%. What should you do next?
scenario.expected_response: I should undertake targeted revision focusing on areas I didn't score well, then retake the assessment. I must ensure both attempts are documented accurately as per policy.

quiz.question: What must an employee do if they score below 80% on a mandatory knowledge assessment?
options: Undertake targeted revision and reattempt the assessment, recording all results.
Ignore the result and proceed with no further action.
Retake the assessment immediately without revision.
quiz.explanation: Employees must score at least 80 percent on mandatory knowledge assessments. A failed attempt requires targeted revision and another attempt; the original result must remain recorded.
quiz.evidence_quote: Employees must score at least 80 percent on mandatory knowledge assessments. A failed attempt requires targeted revision and another attempt; the original result must remain recorded.

rubric.criterion: Explains the required score and revision process.
Describes documentation of all assessment results.
Completes practical assessment and revision plan properly.

items.source_quote: Employees must request correction of an inaccurate attendance entry within 2 working days of discovering it. HR must retain the original value and the evidence supporting correction.
items.learning_objective: Enable HR to manage attendance correction requests promptly and maintain proper records.
items.practical_activity: Simulate processing an attendance correction request received within 2 working days. Document the original entry and evidence supporting correction, and create a correction record.
items.lesson: Employees must request corrections to inaccurate attendance entries within 2 working days of discovering the error. HR is responsible for retaining the original attendance value along with all evidence supporting the correction. Timely and accurate handling of these requests ensures integrity in attendance records and compliance with company policy.
checklist: Identify the 2 working day window to request corrections.
Learn how to retain original attendance entries.
Collect and store supporting evidence for corrections.
Update records while preserving audit trails.

scenario.prompt: An employee informs you of an attendance error discovered yesterday. How should you respond?
scenario.expected_response: I should verify the original attendance entry, retain it along with any evidence the employee provides, and process the correction since the request is within 2 working days.

quiz.question: Within what timeframe must employees request correction of an inaccurate attendance entry?
options: Within 2 working days of discovering it.
Within 5 calendar days.
Within 24 hours only.
quiz.explanation: Employees must request correction of an inaccurate attendance entry within 2 working days of discovering it. HR must retain the original value and the evidence supporting correction.
quiz.evidence_quote: Employees must request correction of an inaccurate attendance entry within 2 working days of discovering it. HR must retain the original value and the evidence supporting correction.

rubric.criterion: Accurately states the 2 working day correction request window.
Demonstrates proper retention of original entries and evidence.
Completes correction processing simulation correctly.

items.source_quote: Document owners must link each revision to the superseded version and identify changed sections. Employees must use the version effective on the date of the activity; historical copies remain available for audit.
items.learning_objective: Ensure HR understands version linking, change identification, and correct version usage for compliance and audit readiness.
items.practical_activity: Review a set of document versions and create a record linking a new revision to its superseded version, identifying changed sections and confirming correct version use for a given date.
items.lesson: When documents are revised, owners must link new revisions to the superseded version and clearly identify which sections have changed. Employees must always use the version effective on the date of any activity, ensuring historical copies are maintained and accessible for audits. This practice ensures traceability and compliance with recordkeeping standards.
checklist: Understand how to link document revisions properly.
Identify and document changed sections in revisions.
Use the effective document version for the date of activity.
Maintain availability of historical document copies for audits.

scenario.prompt: You need to use a policy document for a procedure from last month. Which version do you use and how do you verify its accuracy?
scenario.expected_response: I use the version effective on the procedure date last month and confirm it is linked to its superseded version showing changes. Historical versions remain accessible for audit purposes.

quiz.question: What must employees do regarding document versions when performing activities?
options: Use the version effective on the activity date and maintain historical copies for audits.
Always use the latest document version regardless of date.
Discard old versions once a new revision is published.
quiz.explanation: Document owners must link each revision to the superseded version and identify changed sections. Employees must use the version effective on the date of the activity; historical copies remain available for audit.
quiz.evidence_quote: Document owners must link each revision to the superseded version and identify changed sections. Employees must use the version effective on the date of the activity; historical copies remain available for audit.

rubric.criterion: Explains version linking and change identification accurately.
Identifies correct version use by date in scenario.
Completes version linking practical activity correctly.

items.source_quote: The duty Operations Manager must appoint an incident lead and record the handover. IT leads technical containment while the incident lead coordinates business decisions and communications.
items.learning_objective: Clarify the roles of Operations Manager, incident lead, and IT in incident management for proper escalation and communication.
items.practical_activity: Simulate the initiation of an incident where you document appointment of the incident lead by the Operations Manager, specify IT’s technical containment role, and plan business communication coordination.
items.lesson: In the event of an incident, the Operations Manager on duty must appoint a single incident lead and document the handover process. While IT personnel manage the technical containment of the incident, the appointed incident lead is responsible for coordinating business decisions and communication. This separation of roles ensures clear accountability and efficient handling of incidents.
checklist: Understand the Operations Manager's duty to appoint and record the incident lead.
Recognize IT's responsibility for technical containment.
Know the incident lead’s role in business decisions and communications.
Document the handover and roles clearly.

scenario.prompt: An incident occurs. What roles must be assigned and how should responsibilities be divided?
scenario.expected_response: The Operations Manager must appoint and record an incident lead. IT handles technical containment, while the incident lead manages business decisions and communications.

quiz.question: Who is responsible for coordinating business decisions during an incident?
options: The incident lead appointed by the Operations Manager.
The IT team alone.
Any available staff member.
quiz.explanation: The duty Operations Manager must appoint an incident lead and record the handover. IT leads technical containment while the incident lead coordinates business decisions and communications.
quiz.evidence_quote: The duty Operations Manager must appoint an incident lead and record the handover. IT leads technical containment while the incident lead coordinates business decisions and communications.

rubric.criterion: Describes clear appointment and handover process.
Differentiates IT and incident lead responsibilities.
Completes incident coordination simulation accurately.

items.source_quote: Employees must delete approved temporary customer-data exports within 24 elapsed hours after the approved task ends. A documented preservation hold suspends deletion only for the records identified in that hold.
items.learning_objective: Understand and perform the deletion of temporary customer-data exports within the required 24-hour window following task completion, and recognize conditions suspending deletion.
items.practical_activity: Simulate deleting approved temporary customer-data exports from a test database within 24 hours after completing the task and identify records under a preservation hold to suspend deletion.
items.lesson: This module teaches the critical compliance requirement that employees must remove approved temporary customer-data exports within 24 elapsed hours after the approved task ends to protect customer privacy. Importantly, deletion is suspended only for records identified under a documented preservation hold, meaning only specific data must be kept beyond the 24-hour limit. Failure to meet this 24-hour deletion window risks data compliance violations and customer trust breaches.
checklist: Review the approved temporary customer-data export tasks assigned.
Identify and verify the completion time of each approved task.
Confirm if any records fall under a documented preservation hold.
Delete all approved temporary exports not under preservation hold within 24 hours after task completion.

scenario.prompt: You are overseeing a temporary export of customer data for a report due today, which completed exactly 20 hours ago. You need to ensure compliance with company data retention policies. What should you do next?
scenario.expected_response: I must delete the approved temporary customer-data exports related to the task since it is within 24 elapsed hours after task completion. However, if any records are under a documented preservation hold, I will not delete those specific records.

quiz.question: According to the policy, when must approved temporary customer-data exports be deleted?
options: Within 24 elapsed hours after the approved task ends.
Immediately after task completion.
Within 7 calendar days after the approved task ends.
Only when a preservation hold does not apply.
quiz.explanation: The policy states that employees must delete approved temporary customer-data exports within 24 elapsed hours after the approved task ends, and a documented preservation hold suspends deletion only for the records identified in that hold.
quiz.evidence_quote: Employees must delete approved temporary customer-data exports within 24 elapsed hours after the approved task ends. A documented preservation hold suspends deletion only for the records identified in that hold.

rubric.criterion: Accurately identifies deletion timing for data exports
Correctly applies preservation hold exceptions
Completes practical deletion activity correctly and timely

items.source_quote: Employees must complete the relevant prerequisite training before independently performing restricted tasks. A manager may arrange supervised practice but must not mark an unmet prerequisite complete.
items.learning_objective: Comprehend the necessity of completing prerequisite training before performing restricted tasks independently, and understand management's role in supervised practice without prematurely approving prerequisites.
items.practical_activity: Review case studies of tasks requiring prerequisite training and create a checklist for verifying training completion before independent work, simulating manager approval scenarios for supervised practice.
items.lesson: Employees are required to complete all relevant prerequisite training before performing any restricted tasks on their own. This ensures proper skill and safety knowledge. Managers can facilitate supervised practice to support learning but are strictly prohibited from marking someone’s prerequisite as complete until all training requirements are met. This maintains training integrity and compliance.
checklist: Identify which tasks are classified as restricted in your role.
Verify completion of all prerequisite training for restricted tasks.
Understand manager responsibilities for arranging supervised practice.
Do not begin restricted tasks independently without full prerequisite training.

scenario.prompt: You are scheduled to perform a restricted HR compliance audit task but have not completed the required training yet. Your manager offers you supervised practice to start working on this task. What should you consider before proceeding?
scenario.expected_response: I must not perform the restricted task independently until I have completed the prerequisite training. I can participate in supervised practice as arranged by my manager, but my prerequisite training status must remain incomplete until fully met.

quiz.question: What is the policy regarding prerequisites for restricted tasks?
options: Prerequisite training must be completed before independent work, managers may arrange supervised practice but cannot mark prerequisites complete.
Employees can perform restricted tasks without training if supervised.
Managers can mark prerequisites complete during supervised practice.
Prerequisite training is optional before independent restricted task participation.
quiz.explanation: Employees must complete the relevant prerequisite training before independently performing restricted tasks. A manager may arrange supervised practice but must not mark an unmet prerequisite complete.
quiz.evidence_quote: Employees must complete the relevant prerequisite training before independently performing restricted tasks. A manager may arrange supervised practice but must not mark an unmet prerequisite complete.

rubric.criterion: Explains prerequisite training requirements and restrictions clearly
Demonstrates understanding of manager and employee roles in supervised practice
Develops an accurate checklist for training verification

items.source_quote: Employees must assess parcel weight and route before lifting and must request approved handling assistance when the posted safe-handling limit is exceeded. They must not invent a universal weight limit where a task assessment is required.
items.learning_objective: Learn to evaluate parcel weight and route prior to manual handling and appropriately seek approved assistance if limits are exceeded, without arbitrarily setting weight limits.
items.practical_activity: Conduct a simulated parcel assessment with varying weights and routes, deciding when to request assistance, emphasizing reliance on posted safe-handling limits rather than personal estimates.
items.lesson: Proper manual handling begins with assessing the parcel's weight and the route before lifting. Employees are required to seek approved assistance whenever the posted safe-handling limit is exceeded to avoid injury. Importantly, employees must not invent or apply a universal weight limit themselves since safe limits depend on specific assessments per task. This rule ensures safety procedures are consistently followed and risk minimized.
checklist: Locate and review posted safe-handling weight limits.
Assess the weight and route of parcels before attempting to lift.
Request approved help if the parcel exceeds the posted limit.
Avoid setting personal or arbitrary weight limits for lifting tasks.

scenario.prompt: You need to lift a parcel weighing slightly above the posted limit on a narrow corridor. What steps should you take to comply with manual handling policy?
scenario.expected_response: I must assess the parcel weight and route, recognize that the parcel exceeds the posted safe-handling limit, and request approved handling assistance. I must not apply my own universal weight limits but follow the posted limits strictly.

quiz.question: According to policy, what must employees do before lifting parcels?
options: Assess weight and route, and request approved assistance if the posted limit is exceeded.
Always lift parcels under 15 kg without assistance.
Set their own safe weight limit for manual handling.
Ignore posted limits if the parcel seems light enough.
quiz.explanation: Employees must assess parcel weight and route before lifting and must request approved handling assistance when the posted safe-handling limit is exceeded. They must not invent a universal weight limit where a task assessment is required.
quiz.evidence_quote: Employees must assess parcel weight and route before lifting and must request approved handling assistance when the posted safe-handling limit is exceeded. They must not invent a universal weight limit where a task assessment is required.

rubric.criterion: Accurately assesses parcel weight and route in the scenario
Correctly identifies when to request handling assistance
Follows posted safe-handling limits and does not apply arbitrary limits

items.source_quote: Employees must demonstrate the critical steps of a role task to an authorized assessor before independent work. A numerical score cannot compensate for a failed safety or privacy critical step.
items.learning_objective: Demonstrate and validate critical task steps to an authorized assessor ensuring no failure in safety or privacy steps before independent work is allowed.
items.practical_activity: Perform a simulated role task, highlighting all critical safety and privacy steps, followed by an assessment session where results are reviewed for adherence without compensating failures by numerical scoring.
items.lesson: Before working independently, employees must demonstrate the critical steps of their role’s tasks to an authorized assessor. This demonstration ensures that every safety and privacy critical step is competently performed. Importantly, no numerical score can make up for failing any critical step in safety or privacy; a pass/fail approach on these steps is mandatory. This safeguards workplace standards and protects sensitive information.
checklist: Identify critical safety and privacy steps in your role tasks.
Prepare to demonstrate these steps clearly and thoroughly.
Engage with an authorized assessor for evaluation.
Understand that failing any critical step will prevent independent work regardless of overall score.

scenario.prompt: During your assessment, you miss a critical privacy step while performing a task but score well on others. What is the correct outcome according to policy?
scenario.expected_response: I cannot proceed to independent work because failing a safety or privacy critical step cannot be compensated for by a high numerical score. I must repeat training and demonstrate all critical steps successfully.

quiz.question: What does the policy say about failing critical safety or privacy steps in a task demonstration?
options: A numerical score cannot compensate for any failed safety or privacy critical step.
A high numerical score can override critical step failures.
Critical step failures are ignored if the overall pass mark is met.
The assessor can waive critical step failures at their discretion.
quiz.explanation: Employees must demonstrate the critical steps of a role task to an authorized assessor before independent work. A numerical score cannot compensate for a failed safety or privacy critical step.
quiz.evidence_quote: Employees must demonstrate the critical steps of a role task to an authorized assessor before independent work. A numerical score cannot compensate for a failed safety or privacy critical step.

rubric.criterion: Clearly demonstrates all critical steps to the assessor
Acknowledges implications of failing critical steps on independent work
Completes practical demonstration competently without critical step failures

items.source_quote: Employees must verify the requester using the approved workflow before disclosing shipment details. A shipment number alone does not authorize disclosure of the recipient address or contact details.
items.learning_objective: Understand the necessary verification steps before disclosing shipment recipient details to protect information confidentiality.
items.practical_activity: Simulate verifying a requester using the approved workflow, and determine what shipment information can be disclosed based on verification.
items.lesson: Employees must always verify the identity of the requester following the approved verification workflow before disclosing any shipment details. Importantly, knowing only the shipment number does not grant authorization to share sensitive recipient information such as address or contact details. This policy helps protect the privacy and security of shipment recipients. Always follow established steps and confirm authorization before releasing any information.
checklist: Review the approved verification workflow document.

matrix_snapshot.title: Accidental disclosure

matrix_snapshot.title: Respectful conduct
matrix_snapshot.text: Employees must communicate respectfully and must not harass, threaten or discriminate against another person. A witness must report concerns through the confidential HR channel without circulating the allegation to colleagues.

matrix_snapshot.title: Arrange orientation
matrix_snapshot.text: The HR Executive must schedule core orientation within POL-03 deadlines and monitor attendance. A missed session requires a replacement assignment and visible overdue status where relevant.

matrix_snapshot.title: Knowledge assessment
matrix_snapshot.text: Employees must score at least 80 percent on mandatory knowledge assessments. A failed attempt requires targeted revision and another attempt; the original result must remain recorded.

matrix_snapshot.title: Attendance correction
matrix_snapshot.text: Employees must request correction of an inaccurate attendance entry within 2 working days of discovering it. HR must retain the original value and the evidence supporting correction.

matrix_snapshot.title: Version replacement
matrix_snapshot.text: Document owners must link each revision to the superseded version and identify changed sections. Employees must use the version effective on the date of the activity; historical copies remain available for audit.

matrix_snapshot.title: Single incident owner
matrix_snapshot.text: The duty Operations Manager must appoint an incident lead and record the handover. IT leads technical containment while the incident lead coordinates business decisions and communications.

matrix_snapshot.title: Temporary export removal
matrix_snapshot.text: Employees must delete approved temporary customer-data exports within 24 elapsed hours after the approved task ends. A documented preservation hold suspends deletion only for the records identified in that hold.

matrix_snapshot.title: Restricted work
matrix_snapshot.text: Employees must complete the relevant prerequisite training before independently performing restricted tasks. A manager may arrange supervised practice but must not mark an unmet prerequisite complete.

matrix_snapshot.title: Manual handling
matrix_snapshot.text: Employees must assess parcel weight and route before lifting and must request approved handling assistance when the posted safe-handling limit is exceeded. They must not invent a universal weight limit where a task assessment is required.

matrix_snapshot.title: Practical competence
matrix_snapshot.text: Employees must demonstrate the critical steps of a role task to an authorized assessor before independent work. A numerical score cannot compensate for a failed safety or privacy critical step.

matrix_snapshot.title: Recipient verification
matrix_snapshot.text: Employees must verify the requester using the approved workflow before disclosing shipment details. A shipment number alone does not authorize disclosure of the recipient address or contact details.

matrix_snapshot.title: Protect employee records
matrix_snapshot.text: The HR Executive must restrict sensitive employee records and provide managers only the information needed for an assigned decision. Access requests outside that scope require review.

matrix_snapshot.title: Constructive feedback
matrix_snapshot.text: Employees are encouraged to discuss routine process frustrations privately with their manager and suggest a specific improvement supported by an example.

matrix_snapshot.title: Controlled copies
matrix_snapshot.text: Document owners must record document ID, owner, version, approval role and effective date before release. An unapproved draft must not be used to assign mandatory training.

matrix_snapshot.title: Approved fallback
matrix_snapshot.text: Employees must use only the approved numbered fallback forms or controlled offline register during an outage. Personal notebooks and unapproved messaging groups must not hold customer records.

matrix_snapshot.title: Suspicious content
matrix_snapshot.text: Employees must report suspicious links, attachments or unexpected authentication requests to IT without opening them. If already opened, the employee must report the action and follow the incident process in POL-09.

matrix_snapshot.title: Screen lock
matrix_snapshot.text: Employees must lock an unattended workstation immediately and configure automatic locking after no more than 5 minutes of inactivity. Shared warehouse terminals follow the same limit.

matrix_snapshot.title: Continuity activation
matrix_snapshot.text: Only the duty Operations Manager may activate the continuity procedure after assessing service impact. If immediate danger exists, employees must take the safety actions in POL-08 without waiting for activation.

matrix_snapshot.title: Planned absence notice
matrix_snapshot.text: Employees must submit a planned absence request at least 3 working days before the proposed start. The manager may approve shorter notice only after recording a coverage arrangement.

matrix_snapshot.title: Non retaliation
matrix_snapshot.text: Managers must not disadvantage a person for raising a good-faith concern or participating in an investigation. Any alleged retaliation must be referred to the Managing Director.

matrix_snapshot.title: Emergency evacuation

matrix_snapshot.title: Visitor escort

matrix_snapshot.title: Privacy requests
matrix_snapshot.text: Employees must log access, correction or deletion requests and refer them to the Operations Manager on the same working day. Employees must not promise deletion before checking preservation requirements.

matrix_snapshot.title: Minimum fallback data
matrix_snapshot.text: Employees must record only shipment ID, action, time and assigned operator in the fallback register. Additional personal data requires explicit incident-lead approval and privacy controls.

matrix_snapshot.title: Security practice

matrix_snapshot.title: Restricted equipment

requirements.text: Assigned record owners must reconcile fallback entries within 1 working day of restoration, resolve mismatches and dispose of temporary copies according to POL-06 and POL-07.
requirements.title: Fallback reconciliation

requirements.text: Employees must use fictional or irreversibly anonymized customer examples in training and demonstrations. Replacing a name alone does not anonymize a record containing a real telephone number or address.
requirements.title: Training data

requirements.text: Employees must obtain Managing Director approval before representing the company publicly or publishing customer-related material. Personal accounts must not disclose internal records.
requirements.title: Public statements

requirements.text: Employees must record actual events and must not fabricate delivery attempts, training completion, assessment results or approvals. Corrections must retain the original entry and the reason for amendment.
requirements.title: Accurate records

requirements.text: Responders must preserve relevant logs, messages and event identifiers without modifying originals. Evidence access must be restricted to the response team and a preservation hold applied where necessary.
requirements.title: Evidence preservation

requirements.text: Employees must use the confidential HR channel to report misconduct. If the concern involves HR, the report must go directly to the Managing Director.
requirements.title: Confidential reporting

requirements.text: Employees must obtain recorded approval before taking planned leave. Submission alone is not approval, and employees must not approve their own request.
requirements.title: Approval before absence

requirements.text: Employees may select an optional development topic after agreeing the time allocation with their manager; optional learning must not delay mandatory training.
requirements.title: Personal development

requirements.text: Employees must transfer personal data only through approved company systems to authorized recipients. Personal messaging accounts and publicly accessible links are prohibited.
requirements.title: Approved transfer

requirements.text: Record owners must retain routine delivery-event records for 180 calendar days after case closure. A documented preservation hold overrides routine deletion until the hold is formally released.
requirements.title: Routine operational retention

requirements.text: Employees must refer records with no applicable retention category to the Operations Manager before deletion. They must not infer a deadline from an unrelated record type.
requirements.title: Retention uncertainty

requirements.text: Teams are encouraged to rehearse one incident scenario each month and document a specific improvement to the response procedure.
requirements.title: Response rehearsal

requirements.text: HR must assign an onboarding plan based on role, experience, location and applicable requirements. Prior experience may change practice difficulty but must not remove mandatory acknowledgements.
requirements.title: Individual plan

requirements.text: Employees must access and collect only the customer fields needed for an assigned task. Full identity documents must not be requested for routine parcel tracking.
requirements.title: Minimum necessary data

requirements.text: The first available responder must create an incident record containing observed facts, discovery time, affected services and initial actions. Speculation must be labelled and credentials must be excluded.
requirements.title: Incident record

requirements.text: The HR Executive may invite feedback after the first month and summarize improvement themes without exposing individual sensitive details.
requirements.title: Collect onboarding feedback

requirements.text: During an activated continuity event, the incident lead must issue an internal status checkpoint at least every 30 elapsed minutes until normal service resumes. A checkpoint must state current impact, owner and next update time.
requirements.title: Outage checkpoints

requirements.text: Record owners must correct errors through an auditable amendment recording author, time and reason. Original transaction values must not be overwritten without history.
requirements.title: Record correction

requirements.text: Employees must pause the affected activity and ask the document owner when two equally authoritative instructions conflict or a necessary limit is missing. The owner must record the resolution before work resumes.
requirements.title: Unclear requirements

requirements.text: Employees are encouraged to discuss anticipated leave early so teams can plan coverage before a formal request is submitted.
requirements.title: Calendar planning

requirements.text: Managers must confirm required operational coverage before approving concurrent absences. If coverage cannot be arranged, the manager must record the reason and discuss alternative dates.
requirements.title: Minimum coverage

requirements.text: Employees must activate multifactor authentication before accessing email, remote access or systems holding customer records. IT must provide an approved recovery method rather than disabling the requirement.
requirements.title: Multifactor authentication

requirements.text: Record owners must use approved disposal methods and retain a disposal log identifying category, date range, authorization and completion date. Disposal must not expose readable personal data.
requirements.title: Secure disposal

requirements.text: The HR Executive must map the current approved role requirements to each joining employee and identify any location or temporary-role conditions. Unresolved applicability must go to the requirement owner.
requirements.title: Assign requirements

requirements.text: Employees must disclose a personal or financial relationship with a merchant or supplier before participating in its selection, payment or complaint decision. The manager must assign an independent decision-maker.
requirements.title: Personal interests

requirements.text: Employees are encouraged to suggest improvements to workstation layout or parcel movement after discussing them with the supervisor.
requirements.title: Safety suggestions

requirements.text: Reviewers must verify required evidence before recording completion. Reading a module alone does not demonstrate practical competence or substitute for a required policy acknowledgement.
requirements.title: Completion integrity

requirements.text: Employees must record near misses even when no injury or damage occurs. The supervisor must assign a corrective action owner and verify completion.
requirements.title: Near misses

requirements.text: The HR Executive must notify the manager and IT of an approved role change before its effective time so training and access can be reviewed together.
requirements.title: Coordinate role changes

requirements.text: HR must record each employee role, department, joining date and reporting manager before assigning onboarding. A temporary role change requires a recorded start date, end date and additional requirements.
requirements.title: Role assignment

requirements.text: The incident lead must obtain an IT health check and an operational sample check before declaring normal service restored. A login screen alone is not evidence of end-to-end recovery.
requirements.title: Recovery verification

requirements.text: Employees must obtain IT approval before installing software or browser extensions on company devices. IT must verify business purpose and permitted access before approval.
requirements.title: Software installation

requirements.text: Employees entering marked warehouse handling zones must wear the posted protective equipment. The supervisor must stop the task if suitable equipment is unavailable.
requirements.title: Personal protective equipment

requirements.text: Employees must store API keys and service credentials only in approved secret storage and must not include them in source repositories, screenshots, training examples or support tickets.
requirements.title: Secrets handling

requirements.text: The HR Executive must notify IT of the approved exit effective time before that time and track asset return and access revocation. Urgent exits require immediate coordinated notification.
requirements.title: Initiate exit actions

requirements.text: The HR Executive must retain acknowledgements against the exact policy version shown to the employee. A policy replacement requires evaluation of whether renewed acknowledgement is necessary.
requirements.title: Track acknowledgements

requirements.text: Only the incident lead or a designated spokesperson may issue incident updates to merchants or customers. Updates must distinguish confirmed impact from investigation assumptions.
requirements.title: External communication

requirements.text: Employees may suggest removal of unnecessary personal-data fields from forms, reports or dashboards to the relevant process owner.
requirements.title: Privacy improvements

requirements.text: Employees must classify an incident as critical when it involves immediate physical danger, suspected exposure of customer data or complete loss of dispatch capability. Where severity is uncertain, they must escalate as critical pending review.
requirements.title: Severity classification

requirements.text: The HR Executive must record approved role, department, manager, location and joining date before creating an onboarding assignment. Only information necessary for training may be exposed to the learning application.
requirements.title: Create employee profile

requirements.text: Employees must check shipment and transaction identifiers before entering recovered work into the restored system. Potential duplicates must be held for review rather than posted again.
requirements.title: Duplicate prevention

requirements.text: Training managers must distribute learning across Day 1, Week 1, Week 2 and First 30 Days. Mandatory operational deadlines and prerequisites take priority over a convenient stage label.
requirements.title: Learning stages

requirements.text: Employees must report a non-urgent safety concern before the end of the current shift. An immediate danger requires stopping the activity and alerting the shift supervisor at once.
requirements.title: Safety concern reporting

requirements.text: HR must restrict medical or other sensitive absence details to authorized People Operations staff. Operational managers receive only information needed to arrange work.
requirements.title: Sensitive absence details

requirements.text: The Operations Manager must identify scope, owner and start date when issuing a preservation hold. Record owners must suspend scheduled deletion for the named records until written release.
requirements.title: Preservation holds

requirements.text: Employees are encouraged to arrange a weekly discussion with an experienced colleague during the first month to clarify workflows and identify useful practice.
requirements.title: Onboarding buddy

requirements.text: The incident lead must record recovery evidence, outstanding risks and corrective action owners before closure. The Operations Manager must review critical incidents within 2 working days after restoration.
requirements.title: Incident closure

requirements.text: Employees must use individually assigned accounts and must not share passwords or authentication codes. Service accounts require a named IT owner and must not be used for routine interactive work.
requirements.title: Individual accounts

requirements.text: Employees must follow the latest effective approved policy, then the applicable SOP, then an approved role guide, then an FAQ. A lower-authority document cannot override a policy; unresolved conflicts go to the policy owner before action.
requirements.title: Authoritative instructions

requirements.text: Employees must notify the duty Operations Manager within 15 elapsed minutes of discovering a critical incident. Immediate emergency or containment actions must not wait for a ticket; the notification record must follow as soon as practical.
requirements.title: Critical escalation

requirements.text: Employees must complete core orientation within 2 working days of joining. HR must schedule a replacement session within that deadline if the original session is cancelled.
requirements.title: Core orientation
